lockedMove.speaker: A. C. Grayling
lockedMove.proposition: Natural facts about suffering constrain moral choice and provide a strong basis for mutual respect and kindness.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: pain and everything else and you thought to yourself what should I do about this situation and supposingly the Alternatives that presented themselves were one to go up to them and help them and the other to kick them then you know somehow or other the facts about their situation seem to constrain Which choice you should make and that seems to me a very powerful basis for thinking about mutual respect and kindness

components.text: Argues that facts about another's suffering constrain action despite the evolutionary contingency objection.
Provides a nondivine experiential basis for respect and kindness.

response.rationale: The reply contacts both the evolutionary challenge and divine-foundation claim by arguing that suffering itself constrains choice and grounds humane conduct.

lockedMove.speaker: William Lane Craig
lockedMove.proposition: Natural disasters may be permitted within a providential plan because an omniscient God could coordinate complex contingencies toward bringing people freely into relationship with himself.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: answer that but I think what when can say uh from a Christian point of view is that overall this fits into God's master plan of building the kingdom of God and that in some way these natural disasters and and wars and things of this sort are permitted with a view towards God's bringing the maximum number of people freely into relationship with himself and his morally sufficient

components.text: Supplies a proposed providential structure in which disasters may contribute to freely formed relationship with God.
Invokes a wider kingdom-building purpose rather than compensation alone.
Offers a benevolent-purpose alternative to the initial adverse attribute inference.

response.rationale: The reply contacts the demand for a morally sufficient reason by proposing kingdom-building and freely accepted relationship, but it remains speculative about how particular disasters realize that purpose.
